questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person or entity that is unable to pay debts.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Insolvent**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"insolvent"** means a person or entity that is unable to pay debts owed. (दिवालिया)

 
 
• **Example: **The company was declared insolvent after it failed to meet its financial obligations.
 
 
 
• **"Busted" **refers to being caught in the act of doing something wrong or illegal, or being broken or damaged. (पकड़ा गया)
 
 
• **Example: **The police busted the drug cartel after months of investigation.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the correct word for a person or entity that is unable to pay debts is **'insolvent'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Insolvent**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Insurgent** (विद्रोही): A person who rebels against authority, especially someone who belongs to a group that violently opposes the government.

 
 
• **Example:** The insurgents planned an attack on the capital city.
 
 
 
• **Recluse** (संन्यासी): A person who lives a solitary life and tends to avoid other people.
 
 
• **Example: **After the tragedy, he became a recluse and rarely left his home.

questions.question:
Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence to make it grammatically correct.

Only __the beautiful__ painting is to be displayed in the exhibition.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. the most beautiful .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is comparing one specific painting with all the others in the context of the exhibition.
 
• To express that this one painting stands out as the most excellent, the superlative form "the most beautiful" is appropriate.
 
• In English grammar, the superlative form is used to describe the highest degree of a quality among three or more items.

Correct sentence: *Only the most beautiful painting is to be displayed in the exhibition*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative Form:**

 
 
• **Structure:** Adjective + -er (for short adjectives) or more + Adjective (for longer adjectives).
 
• **Example:** This painting is more beautiful than that one.
 
• **Usage: **Used to compare two items.
 
 
 
• **Superlative Form:**
 
 
• **Structure: **Adjective + -est (for short adjectives) or most + Adjective (for longer adjectives).
 
• **Example: **This is the most beautiful painting in the exhibition.
 
• **Usage: **Used to compare three or more items, indicating the highest degree.
 
 
</ul

The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. enjoyed lunch .

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of a non-restrictive clause, which provides additional information.
 
• The correct form should use **"the lunch that"** to introduce the clause **"he gave us"**.
 
• The structure of the corrected sentence is **"We enjoyed the lunch that he gave us"**.

Correct sentence: *We enjoyed the lunch that he gave us*.

• **Non-Restrictive Clauses:**

 
 
• **Definition:** Provide extra information that is not essential to the meaning of a sentence.
 
• **Example:** The book, which is on the table, is mine.
 
• **Usage: **Separated by commas and do not limit the meaning of the noun they describe.
 
 
 
• **Restrictive Clauses:**
 
 
• **Definition: **Provide essential information about the noun they describe.
 
• **Example: **The book that is on the table is mine.
 
• **Usage: **Not separated by commas and limit the meaning of the noun they describe.
 
 
</ul

• The idiom **"to bury the hatchet"** means to settle a dispute or conflict and become reconciled. (मतभेदों को समाप्त करना और मेल-मिलाप करना)

• **Example: **The politicians disagreed publicly on the new policy.
 
 
 
• **"To seek revenge in the future"** means to plan to get back at someone later. (भविष्य में बदला लेने की योजना बनाना)
 
 
• **Example: **He pretended to forgive his rival but planned to seek revenge in the future.

questions.question: Identify the sentence without the adverbial error.

options.text: She ran the marathon fast incredibly.
She ran the marathon incredibly fast.
She ran incredibly the marathon fast.
She ran the incredibly marathon fast.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. She ran the marathon incredibly fast.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The adverbial error in the sentence is due to the incorrect placement of the adverbs "fast" and "incredibly".
 
• In English, adverbs of manner (like "fast") typically come after the main verb or the object if there is one.
 
• When using two adverbs to describe how something is done, the adverb of degree (like "incredibly") should come before the adverb of manner.

Correct sentence: *She ran the marathon incredibly fast.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Adverbs:**

 
 
• **Adverbs of Manner:** Describe how something happens (e.g., slowly, quickly).
 
• **Adverbs of Degree:** Describe the intensity or degree of an action (e.g., very, incredibly).
 
 
 
• **Adverb Placement:**
 
 
• **Example: **She ran incredibly fast.
 
• **Rule: **Place the adverb of degree before the adverb of manner for clarity and correctness.

questions.question: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.

options.text: This is a very difficult task to accomplish.
A young boy offered her his seat.
I wish I had eraser to erase all the mistakes in my life.
I have a lot of work to complete.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. I wish I had eraser to erase all the mistakes in my life .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence "I wish I had eraser to erase all the mistakes in my life" is missing an article before "eraser".
 
• The correct form should be "an eraser" because "eraser" is a singular, countable noun that requires an article.
 
• In English, we use the article "an" before words that start with a vowel sound.

Correct sentence: *I wish I had **an eraser** to erase all the mistakes in my life*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Usage of Articles:**
 
 
• **"a": **Used before words that begin with a consonant sound (e.g., a car, a book).
 
• **"an": **Used before words that begin with a vowel sound (e.g., an apple, an idea).
 
• **"the": **Used when referring to something specific or previously mentioned (e.g., the dog, the answer).
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Rahul speaks fluently English / although he makes / quite a lot of mistakes /while writing.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. Rahul speaks fluently English .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The segment **"Rahul speaks fluently English"** contains a grammatical error.
 
• The correct placement of the adverb in this sentence would be **"Rahul speaks English fluently"**.
 
• This is because the adverb **"fluently"** should modify the verb phrase **"speaks English"**, and it is conventionally placed after the object of the verb.

Correct sentence: *Rahul speaks English fluently, although he makes quite a lot of mistakes while writing.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adverb placement rules:**
 
 
• **Adverbs of manner** (e.g., fluently, quickly, slowly) are typically placed at the end of a sentence or clause.
 
• For example:
 
 
• She sings beautifully. (Correct)
 
• She beautifully sings. (Incorrect)
 
 
 
 
 
• **Common errors with adverbs:**
 
 
• Adverbs should not disrupt the natural flow of a sentence. Placing them incorrectly can lead to confusion or awkward phrasing.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

As the orchestra played, the audience was __mesmerised__ by the beautiful melodies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'abstracted'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mesmerised means being completely captivated, fascinated, or absorbed by something, often to the point of being almost entranced.
 
• Abstracted refers to being mentally preoccupied or distracted, not focused, which is the opposite of being captivated or fully engaged.
 
• While mesmerised implies deep engagement, abstracted suggests a lack of attention or focus, making it an effective antonym.
 
• The emotional engagement involved in being mesmerised is replaced by a mental detachment when someone is abstracted.
 
• In this context, the word “abstracted” reflects a state of not being completely present, contrasting the absorption in the music.

Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 4'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Alienated refers to a feeling of isolation or separation from a group or situation, which doesn’t directly oppose being captivated.
 
• Dirty describes physical uncleanliness and does not relate to being mesmerised in a mental or emotional sense.
 
• Turbid means something that is unclear or muddy, which doesn’t oppose the concept of being completely absorbed or fascinated either.
